target_customer: Mobile designers and developers who wanted to style and prototype native apps
problem: Designing native mobile UI required slow code changes; designers wanted CSS-like styling and fast prototypes with native feel.
business_model: Paid developer tools: Pixate Engine and Studio licenses, later a cloud subscription
product_category: Mobile app prototyping and styling engine

founders.name: Paul Colton
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO; a Next Web piece says prior companies sold to Adobe, Appcelerator and HootSuite (from a search snippet, not opened, so not recorded).

founders.name: Kevin Lindsey
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page as lead architect.

exit.reason: Joined Google's design team; Pixate discontinued Oct 31, 2016

technical_complexity.rationale: A CSS-based styling engine and SVG renderer for iOS native controls was real engineering, with later Android and Mac ports.

defensibility.rationale: Prototyping tools such as Framer, Origami and Proto.io emerged, and the engine was a developer library rather than a networked product.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google acquired Pixate in July 2015 and made Studio free; the product was discontinued in October 2016.

market_need_then: Mobile app design was booming in 2012 and developers wanted faster UI iteration; the Kickstarter campaign passed its 25K goal.

branding.domain_note: Owned pixate.com, which later became a shutdown notice.
branding.community_and_virality: A 2012 Kickstarter drew criticism: The Next Web asked whether paid sponsorship of the campaign was astroturfing, and a developer blog criticized the campaign being reset with a lower goal.

brand_strength.rationale: Known among iOS developers, but early press about the brand was the Kickstarter controversy and no mascot or community was found.

outcome_analysis: Pixate raised a small Kickstarter round and a 3.8 million dollar Accel Series A in 2013, shipped an iOS styling engine and prototyping Studio, and was acquired by Google in July 2015 to join its design team. Google made Studio free and then discontinued the product on October 31, 2016, so the exit was a team and technology acquisition.
notes: pixate.com is now a farewell notice. Funding coverage is marked complete based on TechCrunch and the press release plus the YC seed; YC deal amount not reported. Kickstarter total of 60K is from TechCrunch (half from the three strategic investors at 10K each). Competition: dated sources near May 2012 were not found; Framer, Origami and Proto.io appear only in 2015 comparisons, so the list is empty. Founder education and prior employers not found.
